CONSEQUENCES: The gsk3b 0.290 best / 0.145 AUC is NOT a defensible scientific result and must not be reported as one.
A donor-region memory seeded by score rank would AMPLIFY the pathology on predictor-backed oracles.
This is upstream of the jump mechanism: move SIZE was never the binding constraint on gsk3b; the search was in a garbage region of chemical space.
r(score, heavy_atoms) is +0.67 to +0.81 on ALL three tasks, so there is a universal size gradient a scale-learning memory could trivially latch onto.

The architectural fix is a proposal distribution grounded in real chemistry (task-independent structural prior), NOT a QED/SA filter -- a filter is a patch, and where QED is the objective it would be uncounted objective evaluation.
FINDING: On gsk3b the search REWARD-HACKS a fingerprint-based RandomForest: score correlates NEGATIVELY with QED (-0.433) and POSITIVELY with SA (+0.684). Its top-scoring molecule carries bare phosphorus, hypervalent [IH] and a peroxide-hydrazine chain at QED 0.03 / SA 7.81. The two similarity/descriptor oracles are NOT fooled -- their correlations run the healthy way and their top molecules are chemically reasonable. So this is oracle-class-specific, not a universal COMPOSE defect.
WHY_IT_HAPPENS: COMPOSE's executor is validity-closed in the VALENCE sense -- every committed state is a complete valid connected molecule -- which is NOT the same as chemically sensible. The proposal distribution carries no prior over real chemistry, so it explores valence-legal but drug-implausible space, and a fingerprint predictor gives that space partial credit. GenMol and InVirtuoGen generate from learned distributions over real molecules (SAFE/fragment tokens) and structurally cannot easily emit [IH]OOCNNCO, so they do not meet this failure mode.
method: final-round snapshot observations of the completed PMO-v2 3x250 run; every scored endpoint re-scored offline for QED/SA/heavy atoms. No oracle was called.
